name: Skewbald
label: Dischord
lede: Minor Threat with a new guitarist and a new name, or two names, since Ian and Jeff never agreed: one studio session, zero shows, and a tape traded around the country, sometimes as lost Minor Threat.

eras.title: Minor Threat, minus a guitarist
eras.text: In the fall of 1981 Minor Threat, D.C.'s biggest band, stopped because guitarist Lyle Preslar went to college. Singer Ian MacKaye and drummer Jeff Nelson didn't stop playing: they went down to the Dischord House basement and started Skewbald.

years.p: Lyle Preslar goes off to Northwestern University and [[Minor Threat|09037f07-42bc-46ac-a1ee-37f834451fee]] breaks up. [[Ian MacKaye|c12f644b-1066-4ead-b0dd-d0c380f5cca2]] and [[Jeff Nelson|51f7994c-949d-4dbe-89eb-2c33f42a5620]] keep playing.

years.h: Skewbald practice in the Dischord House basement
years.p: Ian MacKaye sings, Jeff Nelson drums, [[Eddie Janney|323dd1dd-23e4-45ce-9aa9-c5492096d604]] of the [[Untouchables|16d88df0-a2a9-4b3b-87ff-84e90e312d40]] plays guitar, and [[John Falls|44fd383a-ff3f-4028-8cc9-b01b71f5b2dc]], who'd played guitar briefly in [[Youth Brigade|7029a4cb-83bc-4e5e-8d94-af9caefc453c]], picks up the bass.

q: The band ended up having two names.
years.h: Skewbald or Grand Union: MacKaye and Nelson never agree
years.p: Jeff Nelson names the band Grand Union, after a nearby grocery store. Ian MacKaye finds skewbald in a dictionary, likes it better, and neither gives in.
years.xp: Wikipedia calls it a friendly dispute, and it was never settled. Dischord's answer was to use both, which is why the record and the band page still say Skewbald/Grand Union.

years.p: Dischord thinks the only people who ever saw Skewbald may have been Eric and Toni of Red C, watching a practice.

eras.title: Back to Minor Threat
eras.text: Skewbald shrank to a trio and then disappeared, because Minor Threat came back.

years.h: John Falls leaves; Ian MacKaye moves to bass
years.p: After the Inner Ear session John Falls leaves Skewbald. MacKaye switches from vocals to bass, and he, Jeff Nelson and Eddie Janney practice as a trio for a short while.

years.h: Minor Threat reform, and Skewbald ends
years.p: Minor Threat decide to get back together in April, and Skewbald is over. Eddie Janney goes on to [[Faith|f735a867-9a16-451f-8f83-669ed42e2574]] and later [[Rites of Spring|b2ff1a6d-9198-4646-b068-8965242d245b]].

eras.title: Not a Minor Threat bootleg
eras.text: For a decade the Inner Ear tape moved around the country hand to hand, often labeled as something it wasn't. Dischord finally put it out, and made a point of the catalog number.

years.h: Skewbald's 1981 session finally comes out as Dischord No. 50
years.p: Skewbald recorded three untitled songs with [[Don Zientara|a495882b-4585-4295-9269-e30c63f279fe]] at Inner Ear in November 1981. A decade later Dischord put them out as its 50th release, a one-sided clear 7-inch.
years.xp:
Before this the songs traveled on dubbed cassettes, and Dischord says they were sometimes mistaken for unreleased [[Minor Threat|09037f07-42bc-46ac-a1ee-37f834451fee]]. The same session produced [[Rozzlyn Rangers|941e77e7-46b5-41e6-8260-79f0717bfc33]], the Dischord House theme song.

Three songs went in and two tracks came out: Wikipedia says two were joined as the first track, unofficially titled Sorry / Change for the Same, with You're Not Fooling Me as the second.

years.p: Skewbald's 2 Songs EP gets a CD reissue in October 1997, according to Wikipedia.
Skewbald, the band that never played a show, gets a spot on Dischord's 20th anniversary box set.
